prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, which opened the 10^-18 regime of atomic timekeeping and precision measurement

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B035 alone, credited to Katori and Ye. Having read the full first-round exchange, the chair's first question is the one that matters, so I will answer it directly. What makes lattice clocks a distinct step from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize is a specific physical construction: a magic-wavelength lattice cancels the light shift of the clock transition to first order while holding the atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once without Doppler or recoil shifts. That trades the single-ion's statistical limit for a large-ensemble one and brought stability to a level that makes the 10^-18 systematic floor measurable at all. The comb is the counting tool, and Wineland's ion control is a different route to a different kind of clock; neither contains this idea. Second, the citation should rest on both parts of the achievement, the magic-wavelength concept and the demonstrated 10^-18 performance, because that is exactly the idea-plus-realisation structure that supports two names and keeps Ye's credit tied to the lattice clock and not to his wider comb and ultracold-matter programme. Third, on maturity, independent reproduction and routine inter-laboratory comparisons already exist at JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST, so the case does not depend on the redefinition of the second. That redefinition would strengthen it but is not required. I see no need for a second part: seven of eight members converge on B035 and the other parts proposed are not endorsed by anyone but their proposer.
statement.case_against: The reservation I cannot remove is overlap and attribution. A sceptic can still say that lattice clocks sit in a line already honoured twice, and that Ye's contribution is partly the continuation of a programme recognised in 2005. Lemonde, Takamoto, Lisdat and the Sr and Yb groups at SYRTE, PTB and NIST contributed materially to the accuracy records, and a two-name prize cannot express that; the wording 'invention and realisation' limits the claim but does not erase the omission. I also hold that B008 is arguably the larger conceptual idea. I prefer B035 because its credit can be defended on the historical record, and I would not want a clean attribution to count for more than the science if B008's credit could be resolved. I do not think it can be resolved within three names.

responses.point: Danielsson moved from B006 to B035 on the strength of multi-laboratory reproduction, but cautioned that the attribution is less clean than I implied and that the citation should say 'invention and realization' so a two-name prize reads as a fair statement of the decisive concept and its leading realization.
responses.response: I accept the caution and I do not want to be read as calling the attribution uncontested. My claim is narrower: it is the cleanest on this shortlist, not clean in absolute terms. The citation wording you propose is the right safeguard and I adopt it. I would add the 10^-18 regime so that the realisation half is explicit, because that is what ties Ye to the lattice clock itself and not to the earlier comb programme. Where I still differ slightly is that I do not think the contribution of Lemonde's group or others changes the names; it is a fact the record should state, in the way the committee does when it describes the field, not a reason to enlarge the list.

responses.point: Mehlig regards B035 as scientifically strong but says B008 is arguably more far-reaching, and wants the uncertainty about early strontium groups sharing the idea noted in the record, not used to change the names or break the three-name limit.
responses.response: I agree with that handling and will record it as an uncertainty rather than a reason to change the names. I also agree with your point that a clean attribution should not count for more than the science. That is why I still rate B008 as my principal alternative. The difference between us is small: you weigh B008's conceptual reach heavily and I weigh the three-name credit gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, plus the three-dimensional work) heavily enough that I cannot support it as a public position now. On the strontium point, the idea of a magic wavelength is Katori's, and the first realisations and the performance frontier are separable contributions; two names can reflect that separation.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B008 on the grounds of a new organising principle and a rapid decisive experiment, but concedes the HgTe credit gap and the 2016 overlap and says he would not defend B008 against a well-argued shift to B035.
responses.response: Your concession is the honest centre of this disagreement and I respect it. I share the view that B008 describes a new class of electronic states and that this probably reaches further than a better clock. My difficulty is the same one you name: three names cannot cover the Kane-Mele theory, the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang that made Molenkamp's experiment possible, and the three-dimensional generalisation, and Zhang's death rules out a posthumous remedy. I also think the 2016 overlap is real but not decisive, as you say. If a majority wished to pursue B008 in a later year, I would not oppose it; for this vote I think B035's credit is simply more defensible, and I would ask you to weigh that on its merits and not as a concession.

responses.point: Pearce proposes pairing B035 with a one-name IceCube part for Halzen, accepts that this leaves Karle and Spiering out as a compromise, and says the committee should not add IceCube merely because it is his own field.
responses.response: I appreciate that you state the compromise and the proximity issue openly. I still cannot support the second part, for three reasons. The diffuse flux is established, but the origin of most of it is unresolved and water-based confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD is incomplete, which is the maturity concern Danielsson also raised. A one-name credit in a collaboration-scale discovery leaves out the people who built the detector and the discovery analysis, so the attribution is weaker than for B035, not equal to it. And pairing it with the clock does not strengthen either part: B035 stands on its own with seven members behind it. I also want to correct how my position has been read in places: I have not argued for a particular pair from the IceCube ballot, and nothing in my view depends on the Halzen allocation. I would keep IceCube as a runner-up for a future year, when the source identification is firmer.

responses.point: Olsson agrees on the core case but resists widening the credit simply because the field is crowded, arguing the citation should name the invention and the realization without claiming the whole of optical timekeeping.
responses.response: I agree, and I think this is the principle the committee should apply. Naming Lemonde, Takamoto, Lisdat and the other groups in the discussion is a fair acknowledgement that the 10^-18 level was a community result, but the citation can be precise about what is being honoured: the invention and realisation of the lattice clock. Widening the list would break the three-name limit and dilute the citation. Where I would add one caution to your wording is that 'opening the regime' of fractional uncertainty should be read as a statement about what the lattice made possible, so the citation does not appear to credit the entire accuracy frontier to two laboratories.

uncertainties: Whether two names can fairly express the Sr-clock priority among Katori, Ye, Lemonde, Takamoto and the Yb and PTB groups; I treat this as a recorded limitation of the credit, not a reason to change it.

Whether the committee will accept that the many-atom Lamb-Dicke construction makes lattice clocks distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes; I am persuaded, but the point is a judgement and not a measurement.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second ought to precede the prize; I treat it as supporting and not necessary.
Whether B008 should outrank B035 if the HgTe and three-dimensional credit questions could be settled, which I think they cannot within three names.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with Katori or Ye is documented in my profile. I collaborate with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond group and with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, the institution where Wallraff (B004) works, and I have worked with Reinhold Schuch, J. Marcus Dahlstrom, Luca Argenti and Paul Indelicato. None of these is a direct tie to B035, B008 or B023. B004 is no longer a leading option, so I do not think a recusal is needed, but I would disclose the ETH link again if circuit QED returned as a leading option.
